provenance.name: SMS Spam Collection (UCI)
provenance.citation: Almeida, T. A., Gómez Hidalgo, J. M., & Yamakami, A. (2011). Contributions to the study of SMS spam filtering: New collection and results. Proceedings of DocEng 2011, 259-262.

models.name: Contains a 5+ digit number
models.notes: A one-line hand-written rule: shortcodes and phone numbers. Not tuned on the test messages.

runtime_assertions.name: assert_no_message_in_both_splits
runtime_assertions.detail: 4,136 training and 1,035 test messages after removing 403 duplicates; 0 message texts appear in both.

runtime_assertions.name: assert_naive_bayes_matches_sklearn
runtime_assertions.detail: Spam probabilities for 1,035 test messages from the written-out Naive Bayes and scikit-learn's MultinomialNB; largest difference 1.6e-14 (limit 1e-9).

runtime_assertions.name: assert_gradient_descent_reaches_least_squares
runtime_assertions.detail: Gradient descent (learning rate 0.1, 3,000 steps, scaled features) against the exact least-squares solution: largest coefficient difference 1.1e-16 relative (limit 1e-6).

runtime_assertions.name: assert_backprop_matches_finite_differences
runtime_assertions.detail: All 49 parameter gradients compared with central finite differences, before and after training; largest relative error 1.1e-07 (limit 1e-5).

quiz.question: What share of the SMS messages are spam?
quiz.explanation: 13.4% of 5,574 messages. That is the prior Naive Bayes starts from.

quiz.question: How does this Naive Bayes treat a word it never saw in training?
quiz.explanation: Unseen words carry no evidence either way, so they add nothing to the log-odds.

quiz.question: With duplicates kept, what share of test messages already appear in training?
quiz.explanation: 10.5% on average over 20 splits; after deduplication, none.

quiz.question: Why does gradient descent struggle on the raw power-plant features?
options: Features on very different scales force a tiny learning rate
quiz.explanation: The largest stable learning rate is 9.7e-07 raw against 0.410 scaled.

quiz.question: How is the hand-written backpropagation checked?
options: By nudging each weight and measuring the change in loss
quiz.explanation: Central finite differences on all 49 parameters agree to 1e-07.
